reviews.evidence: Rank-one module operators are closed in the adjointable-operator norm; existing module, norm, and relative-compact prerequisites are sufficient.
The theorem uses a von Neumann algebra, its central projections, and Murray-von Neumann subequivalence exactly as listed.
The core quantifies over linear maps between C*-algebras and their matrix C*-algebras; added the ambient C*-algebra and linear-map prerequisites.
The approximation maps are completely positive contractions; added the CPC definition used by the core.
The CPC definition is completely positivity plus the operator-norm contraction condition, all represented by existing prerequisites.
Complete positivity is defined by n-positivity of a linear map between C*-algebras; metadata matches.
The concrete algebra is a norm-closed adjoint-closed subalgebra of B(H); existing Hilbert, B(H), norm, and C*-algebra prerequisites are complete.
The coefficient-at-identity map is a conditional expectation on the reduced crossed product; all construction prerequisites are present.
The retraction is defined for a C*-subalgebra by a completely positive contractive linear map; metadata is complete.
The core constructs a strongly continuous family of unitaries in a von Neumann algebra; added unitary-element and strong-operator-topology prerequisites.
The Connes type invariant uses type III factors, n.s.f. weights, and modular operators exactly as listed.
Continuity of fiber norms is defined for a Hausdorff C0(X)-algebra and its quotient fibers; metadata is sufficient.
The continuous core is a crossed product by a modular automorphism group and carries the listed trace/dual-action structure.
The core assumes X is locally compact Hausdorff; added the locally-compact-space prerequisite.
The construction assumes a unital C*-algebra; added the unital-C*-algebra prerequisite.
Continuous trace is defined through irreducible representations, positive elements, and operator traces; existing prerequisites cover the core.
The corona is the multiplier-algebra quotient by the essential ideal; metadata matches the definition.
Countable topological generation is defined for a Hilbert module over a C*-algebra; both are present.
The covariant pair uses a C*-dynamical system, nondegenerate representation, strongly continuous unitary representation, and group action as listed.
The convolution formula requires the dynamical system, Haar and modular data, compactly supported vector space, and involution.
The universal generators-relations construction uses universal C*-algebra, star-homomorphism, and supremum norm concepts already listed.
The C*-algebra core imposes the standalone C*-identity in addition to involutive and Banach-algebra structure; added that axiom knowl.
The correspondence begins with C*-algebras A and B; added the ambient C*-algebra prerequisite.
The triple consists of a C*-algebra, locally compact group, and strongly continuous group action; metadata is complete.
Exactness is stated with star-homomorphisms, closed ideals, and quotient C*-algebras exactly as listed.
The standalone axiom is correctly grounded by involutive algebra and Banach algebra structure.
The order is defined from the positive cone in the self-adjoint part and uses the listed partial-order concept.
A representation is a star-homomorphism into B(H), with Hilbert and B(H) prerequisites complete.
The subalgebra definition requires a C*-algebra and norm-closed linear subspace; existing metadata matches.
A C*-tensor norm is defined on the algebraic tensor product of C*-algebras; the existing C*-algebra prerequisite is sufficient.
The construction uses a C*-correspondence, compact module operators, and Toeplitz representations as listed.
Cyclicity is defined for a C*-representation by a vector in its Hilbert space; prerequisites are complete.
The duality theorem uses a von Neumann algebra, Hilbert space, and commutant; metadata matches.
The cyclic-vector definition is grounded by C*-representation and Hilbert-space notions.
The core assumes a factor with separable predual; added the predual prerequisite.
Direct sums are defined for C*-representations and uniformly bounded operator maps; existing prerequisites suffice.
Disjointness compares nondegenerate representations up to unitary equivalence; metadata is complete.
The class uses continuous-trace algebras, Hilbert space, singular cohomology, and unitary transition data exactly as listed.
The Dixmier trace uses a Hilbert space, bounded sequences, and the Marcinkiewicz-Macaev ideal as listed.
A double centralizer is a pair of bounded linear maps on a C*-algebra satisfying multiplier identities; metadata is sufficient.
